section: Unity in the Body of Christ

body.en:
For three chapters Paul told us WHO we are in Christ.

Now he says: LIVE LIKE IT. The word 'walk' in Paul's language meant your whole way of living — every single step, every single day. As a prisoner for the Lord, Paul urges us to live a life WORTHY of the calling we've received.

That is a high standard! Worthy walking means humility — putting others first, not yourself; gentleness — strength under complete control; patience — staying kind even when it is very hard; and bearing with each other in LOVE, making every effort to keep the unity of the Spirit through the bond of peace.

Then Paul lists seven great 'ones' that hold God's family together: one body, one Spirit, one hope, one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all. Seven ones! Whatever differences we have, what unites us is immeasurably bigger.

Unity isn't something we create — it's something we already have in Christ, and are called to KEEP.

verse.en: Make every effort to keep the unity of the Spirit through the bond of peace.

title.en: A Song for Walk Worthy, Stay United

label.en: Activity sheet: Walk Worthy, Stay United

body.en:
Big idea: holy living as the natural consequence of genuine conversion, anchored in unity that already exists and must be actively kept. The four virtues of 4:2 (humility, gentleness, patience, forbearance in love) are not optional add-ons to salvation; they are the marks of a genuinely transformed life. The seven "ones" of 4:4-6 confirm unity is grounded in shared reality, not manufactured agreement.

Conversation starters: (1) 'Walking worthy' — what would that look like in your school tomorrow, specifically? (2) Which of the seven 'ones' surprises you most? (3) What does it mean to "make every effort" to keep unity, rather than just hoping for it?

Pray for one specific step of obedience each family member will take this week to walk more worthily.
